title: The baby who spoke
hookLine: Maryam carries her baby home, says nothing to the accusations, and points to the cradle
last: SHAKE THE TREE; EAT; BE GLAD.

cards: Maryam is walking home: unmarried, carrying a newborn, toward the people who know her family. There's no way to explain this. Any explanation she gives will sound like an excuse.
Under the palm tree she was told what to do: if you meet anyone, say, I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, and I will not speak to anyone today. A fast of silence.
So she walks into town, into the stares, and the voices start. O Maryam, you've done a terrible thing. Your father was a good man.
Your mother was a decent woman. Maryam says nothing at all. She just points at the baby.

teach.h: HOW CAN WE TALK TO A BABY?
teach.b: They're baffled. In Pickthall's words: “How can we talk to one who is in the cradle, a young boy?” And then the baby speaks.

teach.h: I AM THE SLAVE OF ALLAH.
teach.b: “Lo! I am the slave of Allah. He hath given me the Scripture and hath appointed me a Prophet.” His first words aren't about himself as a wonder; they're about who he serves.
Allah has made me blessed wherever I am, he goes on, told me to pray and give charity as long as I live, and to be kind to my mother. Not arrogant, not wretched.

teach.h: PEACE ON ME THE DAY I WAS BORN.
teach.b: Then this line: “Peace on me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised alive!” If that sounds familiar, it should.
A few verses earlier the Qur'an says almost the same words about Yahya, the son of nida'an khafiyya. Two prophets, two impossible births, one blessing. Notice who does the defending.
Maryam doesn't argue or prove anything.

teach.h: SHE KEEPS SILENT; THE TRUTH SPEAKS.
teach.b: She keeps her silence, and the truth speaks for her, from the cradle.
One detail scholars discuss: the crowd calls her sister of Harun, of Aaron.

Muslims understand this as a family or priestly connection, or a brother named Harun, not a claim that she was Musa's sister; a hadith in Sahih Muslim says people used to be named after earlier prophets and good people.
Muslims count the cradle among Isa's miracles, and another surah names it too: he spoke to people in the cradle, and his first words cleared his mother's name.

how: Muslims read the story of Isa speaking in the cradle in Surah Maryam, and his words, peace on me the day I was born, are recalled as a blessing on birth, death and rising.

the town where Maryam's family lived
the cradle, where the infant Isa first spoke

she keeps her vow of silence and points to the baby (19:26–29).
the blessing of peace on birth, death and rising is said of both Yahya and Isa
19:15 for Yahya, 19:33 for Isa, in his own voice.
'sister of Harun' means Maryam was Musa's sister
Muslims read it as a family or priestly connection; a hadith in Sahih Muslim says people were named after earlier prophets.

games.q: you're Maryam, walking into town with a newborn, and everyone is accusing you. what do you do?
o: explain everything, as clearly as you can.
stay silent and point to the baby.
games.why: she keeps her fast of silence and points to him, and the baby speaks: lo! I am the slave of Allah (19:29–30).

practice: Keep a small fast of silence, as Maryam vowed to speak to no one that day: say nothing, and try to say nothing inside too.
When your mind starts drafting a reply, an explanation, a defense, notice it, leave it unsent, and come back to the quiet. If you pray, you can leave your defense with Allah, as Maryam did.

wordCard.voice: Al-mahd, the cradle: where the infant Isa spoke his first words, I am a servant of Allah, while Maryam kept her silence.
